_comment: Exhibitions, newest first. `start`/`end` are ISO dates (America/New_York); the build sorts each entry into On View / Upcoming / Past automatically, so nothing goes stale on its own. Permanent-collection entries use "permanent": true and need no dates.

temporary.title: Forest
temporary.imageAlt: Exhibition poster for Dragana Crnjak: Forest. A large abstract painting in dusty pink, ochre, grey and pale blue, its vertical strokes suggesting trees, overlaid with solid bars of pink, yellow and violet.
temporary.secondaryImageAlt: A painting by Dragana Crnjak: soft vertical forms in muted pink, grey and ochre that resolve into a forest the longer you look.
temporary.blurb: Paintings that treat the forest as both subject and structure, where looking is an active process and nothing stays fixed.
temporary.statement: Painting continues to offer a unique potential to generate new ways of looking, seeing, and understanding the world while reflecting my desire to suspend meaning for a deeper experience of time and presence. It opens a space where cognition begins with the body and the eye, where sensing and perceiving occur before interpretation fully takes hold. I am especially drawn to the space between memory and anticipation, where an image feels both remembered and still emerging.
temporary.bio: Dragana Crnjak is a Serbian American artist and educator whose studio practice is grounded in painting and drawing. She earned her MFA in Painting and Printmaking from Virginia Commonwealth University, and is a recipient of four Ohio Arts Council Individual Excellence Awards in Visual Arts, a Virginia Museum of Fine Arts Professional Fellowship, and a Distinguished Professorship in Scholarship and Teaching at Youngstown State University. Her work has been exhibited nationally and internationally, and is held in collections including Art in Embassies in Serbia and Bosnia, the Akron Art Museum, the University of Chicago, Herron School of Art and Design, Kathryn Markel Gallery in New York City, and the Urban Institute for Contemporary Art in Grand Rapids, Michigan. She is a Professor of Art at Youngstown State University, where she teaches painting and drawing.

temporary.title: Electric Stillness
temporary.imageAlt: Exhibition poster for Ross Pino: Electric Stillness. A painted skeleton with 'rock star' lettered across its skull and crayons for teeth, raising one arm against a black ground scattered with hand-painted stars in pink, yellow, green, blue, orange and purple.
temporary.blurb: Painted figures and hand-drawn stars, loud and still at once.

permanent.title: Renie & James Grohl Collection
permanent.imageAlt: An abstract Alexander Calder composition from the collection: red and blue lines ruled across cream paper, hung with circles, triangles, a spiral and hourglass shapes in red, orange, blue, yellow and black.
permanent.blurb: The James and Renie Grohl Collection at the Medici Museum of Art is a distinguished assemblage of artworks that reflects a deep appreciation for artistic excellence and cultural significance. Generously gifted by the Grohl family, this collection serves as a testament to their enduring passion for the arts and their commitment to preserving and sharing remarkable works with the public.

permanent.title: Carole A. Feuerman
permanent.imageAlt: Sculptor Carole A. Feuerman seated beside one of her hyperrealist works: a swimmer in a lime-green bathing cap, arms folded over a grey inflatable tube, water beaded on her skin.
permanent.blurb: Carole A. Feuerman (born 1945) is an American sculptor and author known as a Superrealist. She is one of the three artists who started the movement in the late 1970s. She is best known for her figurative works of swimmers and dancers. She is the only artist to make realistically painted outdoor sculptures and the only woman to sculpt in this style.

permanent.title: Outdoor Sculpture Garden
permanent.imageAlt: Carole A. Feuerman's sculpture Justice in the garden: a gold-toned figure of a woman in a swim cap and gold swimsuit, seated in a lotus pose on a mirror-polished steel sphere, with trees behind her.
permanent.blurb: Two sculptures donated by Carole A. Feuerman, with a combined value of $1.5 million. “Justice” depicts a serene woman in a graceful lotus pose, balanced atop a gleaming, polished stainless steel sphere — symbolising poise, balance, and inner strength. “Poseidon”, a six-foot bronze completed in 2023, is a permanent installation in the garden.
